newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

SUGAR - World market for August 26 - Raw sugar futures in New York settled just above the day's lows after a volatile and technically-dominated session, traders said. Early speculative buying fuelled the spot- October contract above resistance at 11.94 cents/lb to a high of 11.98.

The market steadied towards the middle of the range and drifted lower for the remainder of the session. October finished 0.20 weaker at 11.65 cents/lb. March closed off 0.11 at 11.35, while the back months ended 0.10 to 0.08 weaker.

Despite the losses, some analysts said the longer term outlook remains to the upside with the spot-October having the potential to climb to around 12.50. The LCE was closed on Monday for a public bank holiday.

INDIA - The Indian government has authorized the Food Ministry to permit exports of 1.0 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 (October/September) season, Commerce Ministry B.B. Ramaiah said. He told parliament that neighbouring Pakistan had sought 208,000 tonnes of sugar from India in 1996/97 (April/March).
In 1995/96 the government had also allowed an export quota of one million tonnes after heavy lobbying from the sugar industry which saw its profitability seriously eroded due to high storage costs.

So far India has signed contracts to ship 911,000 tonnes of white sugar of which 675,000 tonnes had been exported by July. The country will have a record crop in 1995/96 of 16.33 million tonnes, white value.

NETHERLANDS - The third and last Dutch sugar forecast (August 26) for 1996 showed a sugar yield of 9.0 tonnes per ha, white value, up from 8.9 tonnes in 1995, but below the previous forecast of August 12 of 9.1 tonnes, the Institute for Sugar Research (IRS) said. Beet weight per ha was forecast to reach 56 tonnes, unchanged from 1995 but below the previous estimate of 56.6.

The latest computer-generated forecast for 1996 gives the impression that the beet development over the past month has not been satisfactory prompting a permanent downward revision of beet and sugar yields. The latest forecast suggests that the Netherlands will have a below average crop although a result around last year's level of 1.074 million tonnes, raw value, seems to be within reach.

GERMANY - Sugar production in 1996/97 (October/September) could reach 3.868 million tonnes, white value, 1.9 per cent up on the previous year, the German Sugar Association WVZ said. Even though the area sown to beet was down by half a percentage point on the previous year at 515,000 ha, a rise in beet yields to 50.8 tonnes per ha is forecast to result in a overall beet harvest of around 26 million tonnes, up 0.5 per cent on 1995/96.
Average sugar content is expected to reach around 17 per cent. Due to the rather good campaign outlook and satisfactory demand, the beet harvest could start as early as mid-September, WVZ added.

RUSSIA - The fourth Russian beet tests of August 20 confirm that beet development is rather sluggish. Beet weight per ha on August 20 amounted to no more than 18.46 tonnes, up 1.80 tonnes from the previous test compared to a total beet weight of 21.6 tonnes in 1995 after a rise of 3.15 tonnes. The beet yield of the three-year average (1993/95) amounted to 21.30 tonnes after a rise of 3.57 tonnes.

Sugar content on August 20 amounted to 13.1 per cent, unchanged from the previous year but slightly up on the average of 12.8 per cent. This resulted in a sugar yield per ha of 2.42 tonnes, white value, down 15.5 per cent on 1995 and 12.7 per cent below the average value.
Given the rather small number of beets per ha of 65 000 units compared to 68 000 in 1995 and the average of 71 000, the potential for recovery does not seem to be too great.

According to Alexander Nechosov, deputy head of the Semsvyokla Sugar Beet Seed Producers' Association, the Russian beet harvest is likely to be 17.5-19.0 million tonnes this year, after 19.1 million tonnes in 1995.

Nechosov, quoting Agriculture Ministry data made available to the industry recently, said Russian sugar production would fall to 1.85- 1.90 million tonnes from 2.06 million tonnes in 1995. Given the latest rather disappointing beet test results, the lower end of this forecast seems more likely.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports under the 1995/96 (October/September) tariff rate quota up to August 18, 1996 amounted to 1,469,642 tonnes, raw value. This is equivalent to 67.81 per cent of the total quota of 2.17 million tonnes.
